event_name: Eichstätt witch prosecution begins under Westerstetten
significance: Witch prosecution began in the Prince-Bishopric of Eichstätt under Bishop Johann Christoph von Westerstetten in 1617, eventually resulting in approximately 274 executions before ending circa 1631; the Eichstätt prosecution is one of the German episcopal 'superhunt' cluster alongside Bamberg and Würzburg, demonstrating how episcopal territorial authority concentrated prosecutorial capacity.
source_method: Eichstätt episcopal archives; analyzed in Midelfort, Witch Hunting in Southwestern Germany (1972) and Behringer, Witches and Witch-Hunts (2004)
